criteria.quote: Muk needs sludge ponds—cleaner environments may erase it.
criteria.revision: Replace the first line with: “Environmental improvements made Muk hardly seen—and sludge ponds are now being built to prevent its extinction.” This preserves the documented facts while delaying the question of whether the solution can work.

criteria.quote: Muk gathers where sludge accumulates, making the stench even worse.
How could environmental progress push Muk toward extinction?
criteria.revision: Change the open loop to: “If environmental improvements cut Muk’s food sources, can sludge ponds prevent its extinction?” This creates a clearer evidence-based question without claiming more than the research states.

criteria.quote: Environmental improvements cut its food sources, leaving Muk hardly seen.
criteria.revision: Move “MUK WAS TARGETED FOR EXTERMINATION” before “SLUDGE PONDS TO THE RESCUE.” The sequence then escalates from reduced food sources, to extermination pressure, to the surprising decision to build sludge ponds.

Reveal the sludge-pond fact only after the extermination scene, rather than announcing it in the title. The contrast between “targeted for extermination” and “sludge ponds...being built to prevent its extinction” becomes the story’s perspective shift.

criteria.quote:
CLEANUP PUTS MUK AT RISK

Environmental progress hurts Muk
criteria.revision: Replace the first scene’s repeated cleanup claim with the distinct fact: “Muk can be almost undetectable because it blends in with the ground.” Then reserve the environmental-improvement scene for its reduced food sources and declining numbers.

criteria.quote: Now, purpose-built sludge ponds are being built to prevent its extinction.
criteria.revision: Make the final reveal combine the opposing facts: “Muk was targeted for extermination because it scatters germs. Now sludge ponds are being built to prevent its extinction.” This resolves the opening with a sharper reversal than simply repeating that ponds exist.

criteria.quote: Save Muk with sludge ponds, or choose cleaner habitats?
criteria.revision: Replace it with: “If cleaner environments reduced Muk’s food sources, should sludge ponds be built to prevent its extinction—or should environmental improvements continue?” This frames the documented conservation-versus-cleanup conflict more clearly without inventing consequences.
